features.note: 3 blades present at 30% aperture; top blade tips its leading edge forward/down while the middle blade counter-tilts and presents its full convex double-skin airfoil face (matches Ruskin/ref-2 blade read); bottom blade mirrors the top. Adjacent blades are clearly not parallel mid-travel. Scored at threshold because the bottom blade sits mostly in shadow, so counter-rotation legibility rests mainly on the top/middle pair.

Plated drive-shaft stub protrudes from the right frame face with visible free spindle before the black U-clamp grips it; the orange body hangs off the shaft with clear standoff, never flush on the frame — matches ref-1's clamp-near-end mounting, cable gland at the bottom, and a black anti-rotation bracket runs from the lower body toward the frame face.

A pointer dial sits coaxial with the shaft axis on the actuator face, reading as a position indicator. The printed 0-90 arc/tick labels are not legible at capture resolution, and 1:1 rotation cannot be verified because both captures show the same 30% state — presence and placement carry the score, exactly at threshold.

Channel casing shows real depth (~0.13 m return visible on the right face), front flange carries a regular fastener pattern, and a rear flange lip is visible along the top rear edge — consistent with the Greenheck channel-frame evidence and ref-2/ref-3 casings. Galvanized spangle texture reads on the top face.

Exposed vertical tie rod with crank blocks at the three blade-axle heights on the non-actuator (left) side, semantically matching ref-2's crank-and-tie-rod linkage. Simplified vs the stamped cranks in ref-2, and the crank arms do not visibly take different angles for the 30% blade positions, so coherent motion is only weakly evidenced.

important_features.note: Black EPDM strips read clearly along the blade meeting lines; jamb seals at the sides are not distinguishable from this viewpoint.
White label with text block and barcode on the actuator body reads as a printed spec plate, echoing ref-1's labeled housing; text is plausibly printed though not legible at distance.
Cable exits the bottom gland and droops in a believable catenary to a junction box below the frame — clearly not a straight rod, matching ref-1's flexible cable behavior.

defects: Indicator dial reads as an enclosed round gauge; the printed 0-90 arc and tick labels of ref-1's open pointer-over-arc are not legible.
Side-linkage cranks are uniform blocks whose arms do not visibly change angle with the 30% blade rotation, weakening the mechanical-coherence read vs ref-2.
Blade faces read darker and flatter than the galvanized frame; blade-to-jamb seal contact at the sides is not visible.
Both final captures share the single hero viewpoint and the same 30% state, so rotation-dependent claims (1:1 pointer, opposed travel range) rest on one pose.
corrections: Print legible 0/45/90 tick marks and numerals on the indicator arc texture so the pointer reads against a printed scale as in ref-1.
Rotate each crank arm to match its blade angle (opposed signs) so the linkage visibly encodes the 30% state.
